name: fairy boat

sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Fairy boat is a Scottish folkloric motif. Near Scotland, sailors saw a ghostly boat before a storm struck their own craft. One who heeded the warning could haul ashore and survive the weather. One who ignored it probably lost a life at sea. This tradition mixes fairies with the dead. The fairy boat seemed crowded with familiar faces, area men lost at sea who returned to warn old friends. On some stretches of coastal Ireland, people held that no one had truly drowned. The taken were carried off to dwell with the undersea fairies.

okr.objective: Fairy boat is a Scottish motif that yokes fairies with the drowned return.
key_results: The fairy boat is a ghostly craft seen before a storm.
Heeding its warning let sailors reach shore.
It was crowded with the faces of local drowned men.
Some held that no one drowned, for undersea fairies took them.
